correctness.rationale: PASS: the PMP collinearity argument is essentially correct and all computations were independently re-executed. Both symbolic scripts pass: BCH-derived left-invariant frame, brackets [X1,X2]=-X3,[X1,X3]=-X4,[X2,X3]=-X5 with central X4,X5, factorizations x3'=w/2, x4'=x1*w/12-u1*x3/2, x5'=x2*w/12-u2*x3/2, and constant-control ray invariance of P. The adjoint zero-set (h1=h2=0, constant (h4,h5)=(a,b), u*h3=0, h3'=-(u.(a,b))) forces every nonconstant abnormal control to be a.e. collinear u=alpha(-b,a) with (a,b)!=0 (the (a,b)=0 case forces either a constant curve or a trivial lift, a fillable one-line detail), hence s=a*x1+b*x2 is conserved at 0, w=0, x3=x4=x5=0 along every abnormal curve. Conversely constant-control rays reach every point of P abnormally (including e by a go-and-return collinear loop), so Abn(e)=P up to the trivial e-qualification, cut out by three coordinate equations of codimension 3 with Lebesgue measure zero. Sign conventions affect only signs, never the zero sets used.

originality.rationale: FAIL: the exact determination was already published by Ardentov-Le Donne-Sachkov (arXiv:1810.03869, 2018; Steklov Proc. 2019) Theorem 3, which proves abnormal trajectories of the Cartan rank-2 step-3 group are exactly the one-parameter subgroups tangent to span(X1,X2) with projections to the (x,y)-plane straight lines and explicit parametrization x=u1*t, y=u2*t, z=0, v=u2*(u1^2+u2^2)/6*t^3, w=-u1*(u1^2+u2^2)/6*t^3, i.e. manifold A={z=0,v=y(x^2+y^2)/6,w=-x(x^2+y^2)/6}. Up to the polynomial change between their graded coordinates and first-kind exponential coordinates, A is exactly the plane {x3=x4=x5=0}: both are the union of the same horizontal one-parameter subgroups, both cut out by three polynomial equations of codimension 3. The collinearity lemma (u orthogonal to fixed (h4,h5)) and endpoint set are therefore mechanically implied; restating them in first-kind coordinates with the measure-zero corollary is a recomputation/certificate/repackaging of a known stronger classification, not a new claim. A timestamp or failed literal-title search does not establish priority.
